relevance_note: One cohort patient (#15) carries a TNFAIP3 variant: "1 TNFAIP3 mutation (A20 haploinsufficiency, #15 with BD)"; his mother also carries it.
method_note: Cohort of 15 children with recurrent aphthous stomatitis; only #15 (TNFAIP3 c.C1135T p.Q379X) plus his mother (stated carrier) and grandmother (affected, not stated as tested) are in scope; the 14 other patients (STAT1, PTPN22, DNASE1L3 or no variant) get no rows. Spans and rows were assembled by a short Python script from the Table 1 and Table 2 rows copied from the paper; every span was checked verbatim by script. Transcript NM_001270508 comes from the Methods gene list, linked to Table 2 by the legend ('referring to the coordinates of the gene transcript reported in the materials and methods'). The protein change is 'p.Q379X' in Table 2 and 'Q379X' in Table 1. Table 2 'AD' is the inheritance-mode column, not variant origin; inheritance 'inherited maternal' comes from 'HZ(mother)' in the STATUS (carrier) column and the text saying the mother also carries the A20 mutation. Variant type not recorded: the paper never names the class. In silico scores (GERP, CADD, LRT, MT) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Mother's variant row uses the proband's Table 2 row plus 'also carrying the A20 mutation'; her zygosity and inheritance are not stated for her and are left 'not reported'. Table 1 'Age at enrollment (y)' = 16 for #15 is an enrollment age, not age at last evaluation (follow-up continued 6 months after adalimumab), so age_at_last_evaluation is 'not reported'. Onset 0.3 y is the disease onset column. 'usually normal CRP' is hedged, so no elevated-CRP row was emitted; ESR ↑ supports the inflammatory-marker checklist item. Pathergy '–' marked excluded using the legend '“-“: negative result' (the cell uses an en dash, the legend a hyphen). HLA-B51 '–' not recorded (genetic marker, not a feature). Immunophenotype 'N' (normal) for #15 not recorded as a feature; Table S1 lists some #15 values outside the printed normal ranges, while the text says no significant alteration in patients other than #5. Skin abscesses counted as skin lesions; perianal ulcerations and raised fecal calprotectin counted as gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation. Grandmother: 'BD (mother grandmother)' in the Familial history column and 'complaints similar to the nephew' (paper's word); maternal/paternal side not stated; no variant attributed. Table 1 familial-history entries for other patients' relatives are out of scope. is_proband for #15 left null: the paper never calls him proband or index case.

study_type.span: Subjects consecutively referred to the rheumatology unit of the IRCCS Burlo Garofolo with RAS from January 2015 to January 2020 were enrolled in the study.
